research.cross_section: Communist-era showpiece (1984–89, "Victoria Socialismului"), 92 m wide between facades: two one-way carriageways of 3 lanes each (60 km/h) either side of a wide central reservation holding the fountain basins in a long chain (east part continues to ~Bd. Mircea Vodă/Nerva Traian), lawns and linden rows; generous 8–10 m sidewalks with grey pavers, kerbside lindens; restaurant pavilions/terraces (Aici, Altfel, Jo Lounge, Naked Kitchen, Moon, The Clique) along the south side east of the square
research.frontage: continuous 8–10-storey 1980s Civic-Centre apartment blocks with ground-floor arcades, cream/ochre stone & render facades (#D8CDB5–#C9B99A), dark-wood/aluminium windows, balcony rows, pitched/mansard metal roofs with decorative cornices; rooftop advertising letters on several blocks

research.layout: Largest square in central Bucharest; one-way gyratory system (3–9 lane approaches with heavy turn channelisation) around a central park with the fountain field; the square is a concrete slab ("Planșeul Unirii", 32 × 360 m) over the Dâmbovița, which runs diagonally underneath; Bd. Unirii crosses W–E; Pasajul Unirii road underpass N–S (I.C. Brătianu ↔ Cantemir); Piața Unirii metro (M1/M2/M3, Unirii 1 & 2) with many entrances; tram terminal near the SW corner; big taxi rank
research.fountains: 44 independent fountains along ≈1.4 km of Bd. Unirii + the square, >16,000 m² water surface, built late 1980s, rehabilitated by Apa Nova and reopened Sept 2018 with light/music shows ("Simfonia Apei" weekends May–Sept, after sunset); World Record Academy 2019: longest line of synchronised choreographed fountains. Basins: grey granite/concrete rims, turquoise-tiled bottoms, jets 2–15 m.
research.park: lawns, rose beds, linden & birch groups, benches; the round central fountain basin (OSM n1423222582 "Fântâna lui Bucur")
research.frontage: E: Unirea Shopping Center (1976, enlarged 1989; 6 levels in OSM, long horizontal facade with ad banners) + Hala Unirii + Parcare Unirea deck; N: Hanul lui Manuc (1808) near NE corner, Old Town edge; S/SW: Dealul Mitropoliei with the Patriarchal Cathedral on the hill, Sf. Spiridon Nou church (Cantemir); 1980s Civic-Centre blocks (8–10 storeys, cream/beige stone-clad, arcaded ground floors, mansard-like roofs) on all corners carrying large rooftop advertising letters/LED screens
research.works_2023_2026: Since 2023 vehicles >3.5 t are banned on the slab; reconstruction of the Dâmbovița cover started 2024–25 and was in its final stage in summer 2026 (>60 % done, expected end-2026) with restrictions around Pasajul Unirii. Recommendation: model the finished/normal layout (the CV chapter is 2015) and optionally add hoardings at the Pasaj.

research.cross_section: TWO-WAY 1+1 (≈7–8 m carriageway), 50 km/h, asphalt with patches; cars parked half on the narrow (1.5–2.5 m) sidewalks on both sides; no tram/trolley on this stretch; overhead telecom cables and older concrete lamp poles
research.frontage: Bucharest's best-preserved row of late-19th/early-20th-c. merchant houses ("case de târgoveț"): 1–2-storey rendered street houses (nos. 78–111 listed LMI B-II-m-B-183xx, built 1900–1920) with tall windows, pilasters, cornices, carriage gates, many shabby or seismic-risk; interspersed with 4–6-storey interwar blocks (no. 105, 1936; 117-119 S+P+4+attic) and a few 1990s infills; >200 legally protected buildings along the street
research.hala_traian: no. 133 at the Traian corner: Hala Traian (1896) — one of the last two 19th-c. market halls; structure kept but converted into a Mega Image supermarket (red Mega Image fascia on the historic hall); Piața Traian open market opposite (south side)
research.businesses: Mega Image (133), Superbet, Farmacia Dona, myGOLD & Tezaur pawn shops, shaorma, pastry shop, car-parts shops, Bulgust, Toka, Tripoli restaurants (OSM)

top_local_details: Piața Unirii is a vast square on a slab over the Dâmbovița — fountains, park, gyratory, metro, Unirea mall on the east side.
Fountains continue as a long chain in the central reservation of Bd. Unirii; at night they glow in changing colours (shows Fri–Sun in summer).
Bd. Unirii = 1980s Champs-Élysées copy: uniform 8–10-storey cream/ochre blocks with arcades and decorative rooflines; Palace of the Parliament closes the vista west.
Bd. Unirii carriageways are one-way 3-lane each side of the fountain median.
Rooftop advertising letters and LED screens on the blocks around Piața Unirii.
Unirea Shopping Center: long 1970s facade with brand banners, partly empty windows on the north side.
Dealul Mitropoliei with the Patriarchal Cathedral visible from the square.
Calea Călărașilor is a narrow TWO-WAY street, nothing like a boulevard.
Calea Călărașilor is lined by low 1900–1920 merchant houses (listed), many shabby, with a few 1930s 6-storey blocks.
Cars parked on the sidewalks of Calea Călărașilor; loose overhead cables.
Hala Traian (1896 brick market hall) now carries a red Mega Image fascia.
Piața Traian open market stalls opposite Hala Traian.
Trolleybus wires on Str. Traian and Mircea Vodă, not on Călărașilor.
Day Tower glass office + Starbucks and the 12-storey Mercure on Mircea Vodă.
Taxi rank and STB bus hub at Piața Unirii; tram terminus near the SW corner.
Pawn shops (myGOLD, Tezaur), Superbet and a Dona pharmacy along Călărașilor.
Restaurant terraces/pavilions on Bd. Unirii south side east of the square.
Big seismic-risk signs on some Călărașilor houses.
Lindens line Bd. Unirii; old chestnuts/robinias on Călărașilor.
Construction hoardings around Pasajul Unirii in 2025–26 (slab reconstruction).
Heavy congestion at Unirii 08–10 and 17–19, honking taxis.
Biserica Hagiu (1872) near Hala Traian on Str. Traian.
Sf. Spiridon Nou church on Bd. Cantemir south of the square.
Wide grey-paver sidewalks on Bd. Unirii vs narrow cracked ones on Călărașilor.
Metro "M" entrances all around Piața Unirii (Unirii 1 & 2).
Hanul lui Manuc (inn with wooden galleries) at the north-east edge toward the Old Town.
The square is noisy and open — few trees except in the central park.
Mega Image in Unirea basement and Hala Traian; Fornetti kiosk on Bd. Unirii.

Bus stop shelters with STB yellow signs at Bd. Unirii/Mircea Vodă.

driving.note: RO:urban default 50; several boulevards signed 60 (OSM maxspeed=60 on Lascăr Catargiu, Magheru, Dorobanți north).

markings.lane_line: white dashed 3 m line / 6 m gap on urban roads (RO standard SR 1848-7), 0.10–0.15 m wide
markings.centre_line: white continuous (single) on 2-lane two-way, double continuous on 4+ lane two-way without median
markings.zebra: white bars 0.5 m wide / 0.5 m gap, parallel to traffic, no side lines; a few school-zone crossings have red infill between the white bars (verify per crossing on refs)
markings.bus_lane: white continuous line with "BUS" text; since 2019 some STB lanes on Magheru axis/Ștefan cel Mare painted red-brown (#9E3B2E) – verify per street
markings.yellow: yellow only for temporary works and kerb no-parking (zig-zag at bus stops)
markings.wear: markings visibly worn/faded on most streets except freshly resurfaced arteries — use 60–80% opacity

kerbs.material: grey concrete kerbstones 15×25 cm (older streets: granite #8C8C8C), kerb height 12–18 cm, often chipped

sidewalks.paving: mix: (a) grey concrete interlocking pavers ("pavele") #A9A59C on renovated boulevards; (b) cracked asphalt #6E6C68 on side streets; (c) 40×40 grey concrete slabs on 1960–80s estates
sidewalks.parking_on_sidewalk: very common: cars half/fully on the sidewalk on side streets, behind metal bollards on boulevards

traffic_lights.model: RO 3-aspect vehicle heads (200/300 mm), black or yellow housing with yellow-black backplates on main arteries, mounted on grey/black poles + overhead mast arms at big junctions; pedestrian 2-aspect (red/green man) with countdown displays on major junctions

street_name_plates.style: blue plate (#1F4E9A) white text "Bulevardul X" + sector number "Sector 1" in smaller text, on building corners or poles

bus_shelter.style: STB/Clear-channel style glass shelters with grey steel frame and backlit ad panel; many stops have only a pole with the yellow STB stop sign + timetable

metro_totem.style: Metrorex entrance: blue square sign with white "M", station name in white on blue; stairs down with grey stone/steel railings

trolleybus_wires.style: pair of copper contact wires 0.6 m apart per direction at ~5.6 m, carried by span wires between steel or concrete poles on both kerbs (often shared with street lamps)

tram_track.style: standard gauge 1435 mm; on boulevards in a central reservation with concrete sleepers/ballast or grass, kerbed and fenced in places; overhead single contact wire on span wires

lamps.boulevard: galvanised/grey steel octagonal poles 10–12 m, single or double arm, LED or older sodium cobra heads (sodium = orange #FFB45A; LED = 4000 K white #F2F0E6); 25–35 m spacing staggered on both kerbs and often in the median
lamps.side_street: 7–9 m grey poles or concrete poles with single arm, ~30 m spacing
lamps.historic: Calea Victoriei: black ornamental cast-iron style lanterns

trees.species: Tilia (linden, dominant on boulevards), Aesculus hippocastanum (horse chestnut), Acer platanoides, Platanus (plane, older avenues), Robinia pseudoacacia (side streets), Celtis; crown 8–14 m

furniture.bin: grey/green metal municipal litter bins on poles
furniture.bollards: black or grey steel anti-parking posts (~0.9 m) lining boulevard kerbs
furniture.bike: I'Velo green docks at main squares

buildings.ground_floor: shops with mixed signage, many vacant "De închiriat" (for rent) banners; ATM boxes; exchange offices
buildings.air_con: split AC units on facades (very visible)
buildings.cables: loose telecom cables strung between buildings/poles on side streets

gaps: GTS exact office unit at no. 101 (courtyard building?) unverified; registered seat differs (Str. Frunzei 26)
Rooftop advertising brands around Piața Unirii not verified
